Luke Littler, the world's No 1 darts player, has won all the major darts tournaments so far in 2026, and is well on his way to becoming the third man to complete a clean sweep of ranking and non-ranking titles in a single year.
Littler has the World Championship, World Masters, UK Open and World Matchplay titles under his belt already to add to an already crowded 2026 trophy cabinet that also includes the Premier League and World Cup.
He now has to win five more titles to make more history, so Sky Sports analyses Littler's exact path to achieving that historic feat...

What does Littler still need to win?
Littler's next hurdle on the journey to the clean sweep begins on Friday at the World Series of Darts finals.
Michael van Gerwen is the reigning champion, having beaten Littler 11-7 in front of a partisan home crowd in Amsterdam, but the Englishman does have a World Series title under his belt already, having beaten Michael Smith 11-4 in 2024.
Over a week later, Littler will have the World Grand Prix to contend with, live on Sky Sports from September 28 to October 4, where he faces a challenging tie against Luke Woodhouse in the first round.
Littler has previously established that he "didn't like" the double-in, double-out format of the tournament, bemoaning the Grand Prix as "one of the toughest tournaments to win, with the Worlds, the Matchplay, [and] the Premier League".
That format change, though, did not stop Littler from winning 6-1 in the 2025 final in a dominant performance against world No 2 Luke Humphries.
His journey will then take him to Dortmund, where he will seek to win the one major title that has eluded him in his career thus far - the European Championship, where he suffered a 10-7 second-round defeat at the hands of James Wade in the last edition in 2025.
Should Littler win that title, he would hold all of darts' major titles - something no one else has done (as Van Gerwen nearly did it in 2016 and 2017 but did not win the World Cup of Darts).
Littler then would have to win a third straight Grand Slam title in Wolverhampton, before taking a trip to Minehead to retain the Players Championship, where he beat Nathan Aspinall 11-8 in the 2025 final.
If the teenager wins all of those titles, he would become the first player to win every darts major in the same calendar year.
How can Littler qualify for the Players Championship Finals?
Littler has significant work to do on the Pro Tour to stand any chance of securing the Players Championship - and, by extension, the clean sweep.
He is ranked 125th on the Players Championship Order of Merit with just £10,500 in prize winnings thus far - only the top 64 qualify for the finals weekend at Minehead.
Shane McGuirk sits in 64th with £27,500 in winnings with just six Players Championship events in the calendar left, meaning the reigning champion would have to make up at least £17,500 in winnings in order to qualify.
This is still a feasible target for Littler, with the winner of each event adding £15,000 to their kitty - so he probably has to win just one of the six remaining events - and accumulate some prize money in the others - to stand a chance of retaining his title.
The world No 1 was hoping to do much of the work in August, when he returned to the floor events in Leicester after missing the first 26 Players Championships, but he only managed to reach a quarter-final and a semi-final in his two appearances.
Littler will fancy his chances to make up the deficit in prize money with six events in Den Bosch and Leicester remaining - but the clock is starting to tick.

Candy Crush developers are planning a strike for next week
King's staff want to get negotiations back on track after years of bargaining.
Staff at Candy Crush Saga developer King could go on strike next week, according to statements from Swedish labor unions Unionen and Sveriges Ingenjörer. King's developers have been attempting to negotiate a union contract for years, but have now issued a strike notice after their proposed collective bargaining agreement (CBA) was shot down by studio leadership in August, Kotaku reports.
"Our members at King are entitled to secure conditions, a say in their workplace and clear rules that apply to everyone," Unionen posted on LinkedIn. "That is why Unionen is giving notice of strike action." Sveriges Ingenjörer shared a similar sentiment in its own statement, noting that unless union members and King leadership can come to an agreement with a mediator, the strike will go into effect on September 25.
King set the union on this path when it declined to accept its proposed CBA, claiming that its existing benefits were better for all of its global employees, including those in Sweden. Issuing a strike notice doesn't necessarily mean the union will have to follow through, though: the threat of a work stoppage is often enough to get management back to the bargaining table.
Microsoft acquired King as part of its $68.7 billion purchase of Activision Blizzard in 2023. Workers at Blizzard Entertainment ratified their first union contracts earlier this week, winning wage increases, a hybrid work schedule, and "just cause" protections, among other benefits. That success and King's role as one of Microsoft's guaranteed video game earners — King's Candy Crush Saga earned $875 million in 2025 alone, Bloomberg reports — likely adds even more pressure to the contract negotiations.

On August 17, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) announced its revamped social media team, appointing Deepak Mhaskey as the national social media convenor, and Priti Gandhi, Shivanand Dwivedi, Alok Bhatt and Arun Yadav as co-convenors.
While curiosity grew as to who these newly appointed individuals were and their past work and association with the party, social media users were quick to notice that immediately after the announcement, Gandhi, Dwivedi and Yadav made their X accounts private and there was no trace of Bhatt on the internet.
While all the other IT cell members are back to being active on X, albeit after deleting hundreds of thousands of old posts, Alok Bhatt is the only one in the group whose X handle remains inaccessible or ‘protected’ even a month after the new team was announced.
The only remnants of Bhatt’s online presence are the now-disabled X account, screenshots from his X posts and some articles in Right-wing outlets like OpIndia, Organiser and Swarajya.
Alt News found that in the past, Bhatt had been called out for controversial tweets several times. In archived screenshots of his posts from the past, the BJP functionary can be seen using sexist, Islamophobic, and derogatory language, some of which can be seen below:
Who is Alok Bhatt?
Bhatt, who claims to hail from Dehradun, has worn many hats over the course of his career. According to his LinkedIn profile, he graduated from Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University (HNBGU) in Uttarakhand and went on to work with several organisations, including NIIT University, where he served as financial controller until April 2010.
In 2010, he founded Nature Connect Outdoors — an education and adventure non-profit organisation that deals in outdoor education and skill development, including treks, camping, and rafting expeditions. According to the website’s bio, Bhatt had “shunned his corporate career” to follow his passion, which culminated in the formation of the NGO. The organisation is still functional.
According to details available on Zauba Corp, Bhatt is a Chartered Accountant (CA) and the partner of a firm of CAs called RSAC & CO LLP, incorporated in May 2021.
Bhatt has also served as the economic adviser to former Uttarakhand chief minister Trivendra Singh Rawat. However, it’s not clear when he was appointed and when exactly his tenure ended. He wrote an article for Firstpost defending the ministry of housing and urban affairs over the controversial Central Vista project. The author bio designated him as ‘Economic Advisor’ to Rawat.
In 2020, after a district officer’s press release promoting inter-caste and interfaith marriages drew criticism from social media users, Bhatt had reportedly tweeted: “No one from the government has spoken in support of promoting interfaith marriages. No one in the BJP government in their wildest dreams will support anything that is made out here.”
We sent an email and called up Bhatt several times to know more from him, but he did not respond.
Long-standing Association With BJP
Bhatt’s X handle, @alok_bhatt, was followed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In fact, Modi quote-tweeted one of Bhatt’s posts in 2024, where he urged people to watch the film Sabarmati Report.
Bhatt was also invited to PM Modi’s swearing-in ceremony in the past. In 2024, Right-wing influencer Vikas Pandey shared an image with Bhatt alongside former BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma, member of the economic advisory council to the PM, Sanjeev Sanyal, and others, with the caption “First swearing in”.

X Handle Suspended for Violating Guidelines
Alt News found at least three instances, in 2018, 2019, and 2020, where X (then Twitter) had initiated action against Bhatt’s handle for violation of community guidelines, and at least two of those three actions were owing to hateful content.
In 2018, Bhatt declared that all the “killers of Pandits, Rapists of Pandits, Terrorists killing in Kashmir, instigators of Godhra, and bombers of Mumbai were all Muslims, and thus Islam was the problem”. His account had then been ‘limited’.
Why is @alok_bhatt blocked by twitter for a week when blue-ticked racist bigots like Audrey Truschke are still on Twitter despite their naked Hinduphobia? @TwitterIndia pic.twitter.com/3qlnNiVWhj
— Shefali Vaidya. 🇮🇳 (@ShefVaidya) April 20, 2018
In 2019, Bhatt declared in a post that “their boys could take on Jihadis” but needed police action for “rumour mongers” like activist Shehla Rashid. “These jihadi accomplices are running a hate campaign aided and abetted by Media…please help our state dispel rumours,” the tweet read. His account was suspended after this. Political analyst and Right-wing influencer Suresh Nakhua took to Twitter to condemn the move.
Just because @alok_bhatt exposed lies of Shehla Liar Rashid, @twitter has suspended the handle.#BringBackAlokBhatt pic.twitter.com/YJpuOAxQjZ
— Suresh Nakhua 🇮🇳 (@SureshNakhua) February 17, 2019
His account was suspended again in 2020.
What’s this @TwitterIndia ? @alok_bhatt has tweeted about Hindu girls being kidnapped, r@ped and forcefully converted to !slam in Pakistan and his account has been suspended, What kind of nonsense is this? Explain!#BringBackAlokBhatt pic.twitter.com/w4T3epRn6t
— संवैधानिक डकैत (@Shivam_h9) May 29, 2020
The Pamphlet-Savitr Analytics-Alok Bhatt Connection
In 2022, Bhatt took on a directorial role at Savitr Analytics Media and Research Foundation, a company that was incorporated in April 26 that year, with Bhatt and Ashish Nautiyal initially named as directors. According to documents filed with the Union ministry of corporate affairs (MCA), Bhatt holds 9,500 shares, or 95 per cent of the company, while Nautiyal holds the remaining 500 shares, or 5 per cent.
Interestingly, Nautiyal is also the founding editor of the Right-wing media outlet, The Pamphlet.
Savitr Analytics has no website or online presence. We went through its financial records filed with the MCA for the financial years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25, and found that it was registered as a Section 8 company, i.e., a non-profit. In the 2024-25 financial year, its total revenue from operations was Rs 2.7 crore.
The organisation’s revenue across all three years comes from ‘sale of services’, and the rows for ‘Grants or donations received (relevant for Sec 8 companies)’, present in the 2022-23 and 2023-24 filings, are left blank in 2022-23 and 2023-24. In 2024-25, the row does not exist.
Under ‘Corporate Information’, they state ‘Research and awareness about Indian culture and heritage…’, ‘Promotion of commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, and environmental protection…’ and ‘Advancement of education, learning, and skills development…’ as their activities.
There was a category called ‘professional expenses’ in the 2022-23 filing that was later relabeled as ‘content production expenses’. Rs. 41,48,600 was spent in the first year, Rs. 95,36,600 (filed directly as content production expenses) was spent in the second year, and Rs. 1,38,53,200 (also filed directly as content production expenses) was spent in the third year.
Next, we found that an individual named Ridhika Aggarwal stated on LinkedIn that she worked as a content writer for Savitr Analytics Media and Research Foundation until August 2023. We went through her X timeline (linked to her LinkedIn profile) and found that she wrote at least three articles for The Pamphlet during her tenure at Savitr. None of the articles are currently available on the website.
Ridhika is also listed as a non-official member of a steering committee formed by the Union ministry of environment, forest and climate change in 2023.
The Pamphlet, previously known as The Indian Affairs, posted for the first time on Facebook in April 2022, which is the same time when Savitr Analytics was incorporated.
ठीक 2 साल पहले देहरादून में आज ही के दिन @Pamphlet_in ऑफिस निर्माण की शुरुआत हो गई थी, उत्तराखण्ड चुनाव निपटने के बाद मैं २० दिन के अपने नैनीताल और लैंसडाउन प्रवास के बाद दून घाटी में उतरा था।
आज ही के दिन साल 2019 में लोकसभा चुनाव का रिजल्ट भी आया था और प्रधानमंत्री… pic.twitter.com/6lAVSW3twN
— V Ashish Nautiyal (@ashu_nauty) May 15, 2024
The Pamphlet claims to “cut through the noise of the modern information ecosystem by offering readers and viewers clarity, depth and perspective on issues that shape India and the world.” Its reports have seem to be echoing pro-BJP narratives. An August 11 video report, for instance, was captioned: “Questions raised in the public domain regarding the credentials of two CJP leaders, Abhijeet Dipke and Saurav Das, have brought up several serious concerns”. It questioned Dipke’s Boston University degree, academic timeline and funding, as well as Das’ property, tenancy, rent, police verification, and electoral records.
During the CJP protests, another report took a swipe at Mohammed Junaid, who had been feeding protesters, with the reporter noting that “such bhaijaans were also seen” at the protest sites in Shaheen Bagh and Farmers’ stir. Thumbnails of these reports carried AI-generated visuals of individuals critical of the Union government, their faces distorted through AI to portray them in a negative light. This is a tactic common across Right-wing outlets and social media troll handles.
More recently, the outlet, alongside Abhijit Iyer-Mitra, Law Beat, The Jaipur Dialogues and The Sunday Guardian, was summoned by the Delhi high court over a Rs 2 crore privacy suit by Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das, who alleged that they had disclosed his home address and other personal details online. The case will be heard on September 14.
The video below depicts a time when the outlet was still called The Indian Affairs, and Nautiyal (in striped shirt) can be seen with his colleagues alongside educator Pawan Gupta.
The Indian Affairs @ForIndiaMatters Coming Soon
Subscribe our Youtube Channel: https://t.co/orjioxscXy #TIA #TheIndianAffairs pic.twitter.com/v1VVtf83XZ
— The Pamphlet (@Pamphlet_in) July 22, 2022
Nautiyal’s last video with The Pamphlet was uploaded in December 2024. In June 2025, Nautiyal was pictured with the OpIndia team. His first video for OpIndia, an interview with Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Dhami, came a month later, in July 2025.
Nautiyal is now the multimedia & digital head and editor at OpIndia, and is no longer listed as a director of Savitr on the MCA website.
It is worth noting that The Pamphlet’s website does not disclose any parent company, ownership, editorial team, funding details or board of directors. Its ‘About Us’ page offers only a description of what it does, while calling itself ‘an independent digital media platform’. The only publicly mentioned funding source we could find was YouTube memberships of The Pamphlet costing Rs. 119 to Rs. 3199 per month.
Nautiyal is not the only link between Savitr Analytics and The Pamphlet. An individual named Shiv Kumar Mishra was appointed the director of Savitr Analytics in April 2023. In March 2023, Mishra was announced as the CEO of The Pamphlet.
Please welcome @shivkmishr, Founder & CEO, The Pamphlet https://t.co/U53aK62Fzo
— The Pamphlet (@Pamphlet_in) March 14, 2023
In other words, two of the three directors of Savitr Analytics Media and Research Foundation have held senior positions at The Pamphlet. And in both cases, the appointments to Savitr and The Pamphlet came in close succession. This raises the question of whether the two entities are formally linked.
We also found that The Pamphlet had an office space from its inception in Dehradun, and it is evident from a photo posted by Nautiyal that it began with a team of at least 20 people. Bhatt, the reader would remember, also claims to be from Dehradun.
While all of this points to a connection between Bhatt and The Pamphlet, there appears to be a concerted effort to keep that relationship under wraps. Hence, we tried to dig more.
Is Bhatt Linked to The Pamphlet? We Asked The Pamphlet
We sent an email to The Pamphlet on September 3 asking them about the relationship between Savitr Analytics and The Pamphlet, and whether Alok Bhatt was connected to The Pamphlet, given that he holds a 95% stake in Savitr Analytics, a company whose other directors have held senior positions at The Pamphlet. We also asked them about their funding sources, since nothing is mentioned on the website.
In reply, they asked us to send our queries to another email ID of The Pamphlet and also to Alok Bhatt, Nirwa Mehta, Ashish Nautiyal and Shiv Mishra. Interestingly, they provided us with the email IDs and phone numbers of each of these individuals. This, in itself, might be considered an indicator of some sort of link between The Pamphlet and Bhatt. It is unlikely for an organisation to provide the direct contact details of someone with whom it has no professional association.
We then sent our queries to all of them.
Nautiyal responded to us saying that his reporting manager, OpIndia editor Nupur J Sharma, “suggested” him “not to give (you) any quotes or information as a matter of policy of not engaging with entities that don’t act in good faith”. A day later, he took to X to let the world know that a woman from Alt News “with a Hindu-sounding name” had approached him with some questions.
Pamphlet editor Nirwa Mehta sent us a 1,071-word response, but did not answer any of our questions. Instead, she sent a detailed set of reciprocal questions concerning Alt News’ funding transparency, the outside associations of its founders and editor, and grants received by individuals associated with Alt News, both currently and in the past. She offered to answer Alt News’ questions in writing once Alt News answered hers first.
It is worth noting that The Pamphlet published a video on Alt News on August 16, 2026, without seeking a response from the organisation.
This correspondent responded to Mehta, stating that questions concerning Alt News’ funding should be directed to its editor, while questions concerning any of the founders’ personal assignments should be directed to the person concerned. We also reminded her that a so-called expose on Alt News’ founders had been published by The Pamphlet without either of the concerned persons being approached for a response — a violation of basic journalistic ethics.
In her final response, Mehta did not address the question of ethics. Instead, in a demand that many may find bizarre, she asked this correspondent, “as a responsible employee”, to take her questions to the Alt News directors.
At this point, we felt there was no point continuing the conversation.
We will update our article if The Pamphlet answers Alt News’ questions on whether Savitr Analytics and The Pamphlet are connected in any way, and whether Alok Bhatt, BJP’s new IT cell member who continues to remain away from X, holds a position at The Pamphlet.
Social Media Posts Answer the Question
The connection between The Pamphlet and Alok Bhatt is one of internet’s worst kept secrets, it seems. We found several instances on social media where well-known faces from the Right-wing ecosystem tagged Alok Bhatt alongside members of The Pamphlet team — whether to thank them for invitations to Delhi Shabdotsav 2026, where The Pamphlet Panchayat featured on the itinerary, or in connection with other events involving the organisation.
On January 5, 2026, Right-wing influencer Abhijit Iyer-Mitra, who was recently criticised for comparing Newslaundry journalists to prostitutes, thanked The Pamphlet team — including its editor Nirwa Mehta, anchor Shreya Arora, and Bhatt — for inviting him to speak at The Pamphlet Panchayat.
Responding to Iyer-Mitra, Nirwa Mehta and another The Pamphlet employee, Pratibha, thanked him for being a part of the session. The exchange is significant because it can be seen as an acknowledgement by the Pamphlet editor and another employee of Bhatt being a part of the organisation.
Delhi Shabdotsav 2026 was a three-day cultural and literary festival held from January 2 to January 4, 2026, organised by Suruchi Prakashan with the support of the department of art, culture and languages of the Delhi government. The Pamphlet was the digital partner at the event and hosted ‘The Pamphlet Panchayat’ at the fest. The Pamphlet team held and moderated several discussions over the three days, including those with Sanjeev Newar, Vijay Patel, and Subhi Vishwakarma. The subjects of the discussions ranged from ‘Love Jihad: factsheet’ to ‘Bharat’s Hostile Neighbourhood & Need to Regain Shatrubodh’.
We went through the images posted on Shabdotsav’s website and found that Bhatt was present at the event.
The link between Alok Bhatt and The Pamphlet becomes more apparent in another conversation on X in which Iyer-Mitra directly addressed Mehta as Pamphlet and Alok Bhatt’s ‘staff’. Iyer jokingly rebuked Mehta for liking a certain kind of car. Tagging Bhatt, he wrote, “Do @Pamphlet_in and @alok_bhatt @shreya_arora22 approve of these disgusting and extremely hateful statements by their staff?” Mehta responded to Iyer-Mitra’s post, but did not object to the ‘staff’ reference.
On June 1, 2023, a little more than a year after The Pamphlet’s inception, one @saket71 posted a picture with Ashish Nautiyal, who was working at The Pamphlet then, and called him a ‘Media Mughal’. He later tagged Alok Bhatt and Shiv Mishra, praising them for “putting a great team together.”
Such a pleasure to meet the young stars of @Pamphlet_in , @RitikaChandola @himanshi__bisht and the whole team. Such a great young team, full of hope and dreams, and a visible sense of great camaraderie. Kudos to @alok_bhatt and @shivkmishr for putting a great team together. https://t.co/NnmHkA9rQO
— saket साकेत ಸಾಕೇತ್ 🇮🇳 (@saket71) June 1, 2023
Several people have congratulated Alok Bhatt at various points of time upon The Pamphlet reaching certain milestones.
To sum up, what raises serious questions about the BJP’s decision to name Bhatt as its social media co-convenor is not just his past social media conduct, but also the opacity surrounding his professional associations. One organisation he appears to be associated with, The Pamphlet, does not publicly disclose its ownership, editorial team, board or funding sources. Without any apparent source of funding, it starts off as a 20-member organization. Who pays their salary? How are establishment costs met? There are no answers. Again, another corporate entity closely linked to him, Savitr Analytics, has no website or public online presence despite reporting Rs 2.7 crore in operational revenue in 2025.
Things get murkier when one takes into account the desperate efforts by Bhatt’s associates to conceal his association with The Pamphlet, evident in the organisation’s refusal to answer direct questions regarding this.
In other words, a man linked to organisations with questionable records, and whose involvement with a pro-government outlet is abundantly visible in public, but markedly absent from the outlet’s own disclosures, has now been given a formal position in the BJP’s social media cell.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has revised the MBBS seat matrix for the 2026-27 academic year, while cautioning medical colleges and counselling authorities against admitting students beyond the intake capacity formally approved by the regulator.
In a public notice issued earlier this month, the NMC said the updated matrix incorporated permissions granted for the establishment of new medical colleges and increases in the annual intake of existing colleges following decisions by its Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), its first appeal committee and the second appeal committee under the Union Health Ministry.
Not final
The regulator has also made it clear that the latest matrix is not necessarily final. It said the seat matrix would remain subject to revision based on subsequent decisions of the appeal committees or other competent authorities, with any changes to be uploaded on the NMC website and taken into account by the Central and State counselling committees.
The latest matrix lists 1,40,214 MBBS seats across 836 medical colleges, including 63,971 seats in 391 government colleges and 76,243 seats in 445 private colleges. It follows an earlier matrix listing 1,27,028 renewed seats. The latest update includes 13,186 additional seats, of which 10,400 are in private medical colleges and 2,786 in government institutions.
The NMC’s latest warning comes against the backdrop of continuing approvals, appeals and changes in sanctioned intake. It has specifically directed counselling committees not to permit admissions against seats in excess of those approved and notified by MARB.
“Under no circumstances” should any medical college or institution admit students beyond its approved annual intake, the regulator said, warning that such admissions would constitute non-compliance with the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, and the regulations framed under it and could attract regulatory and penal action.
Report any discrepancy
The NMC has also asked counselling committees to refer any discrepancy between the seats being offered by a college and those appearing in the approved matrix to MARB for clarification.
The notice has a further caveat for private medical colleges that have received permission either to establish a new MBBS college or increase their annual intake but have not yet furnished the required electronic bank guarantee.
Such colleges have been given seven days to submit the guarantee in favour of the Director, MARB. The letter of permission will be issued only after the guarantee is received, verified and found to be in order.
The regulatory clarification assumes significance as medical colleges have continued to receive permissions and seek increases in intake through the assessment and appeals process. It also places the onus on counselling authorities to ensure that the number of seats offered to NEET-UG candidates corresponds strictly to the latest sanctioned capacity.
The revised matrix also means that students and counselling authorities will have to track subsequent changes rather than rely on earlier versions of the seat matrix.
The NMC has directed all medical colleges to verify their institutional details in the latest matrix and immediately report any discrepancy or omission to MARB, preferably before the commencement of counselling.
The regulator’s repeated emphasis on sanctioned intake also highlights a fundamental distinction between a college seeking or receiving approval for additional capacity and the actual issuance of the letter of permission. Until the prescribed regulatory requirements, including the bank guarantee where applicable, are completed, the additional seats cannot be treated as available for admission.
The NMC has asked colleges to ensure that admissions for 2026-27 are made only against the seats notified in the latest matrix, “as amended from time to time”.

Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths
- Published
Police in South Africa have confirmed the discovery of a ninth woman's body in just two months, amid growing concern over a string of unexplained deaths east of Johannesburg.
The latest victim was found half-naked and wrapped in a sheet on the side of a road in Dawn Park on Thursday morning, police said. Her identity has not yet been released.
The discovery follows the deaths of eight other women whose bodies have been found since July across Ekurhuleni, a major urban area of Johannesburg.
Several of the women were found partially clothed and with injuries, but police have stressed that they have not established whether all the deaths are connected or whether a serial killer is responsible.
- Abducted South African journalist found dead with gunshot wounds 
  - Published4 hours ago
President Cyril Ramaphosa has vowed that "no stone will be left unturned" in finding those behind the killings, which he said were "causing fear and uncertainty in our communities".
Among the victims was 38-year-old Elizabeth "Tsontso" Moselakgomo, who disappeared last week after leaving her home for an afternoon run. Her body was found three days later behind a hotel in Kempton Park.
Two other victims have since been identified as Itumeleng Kekana, who had been missing since July, and 38-year-old Dineo Evelyn Motapane, whose body was discovered by the roadside in KwaThema on Tuesday.
The first of the nine bodies was discovered in Kempton Park on 15 July. A suspect was arrested two days later in connection with that case and remains in custody, but police have not linked that suspect to the other deaths.
Further bodies were discovered in August and September, including in Kempton Park, Olifantsfontein, Clayville and KwaThema.
The latest body is of a woman believed to be in her 30s and appeared to have bruises and stab wounds, local media reported.
Police have assembled a multidisciplinary team of detectives, intelligence officers, forensic experts and other specialists to investigate the deaths and establish whether there are links between the cases.
They are also pursuing a person of interest, although they have not disclosed which case or cases that person may be connected to.
"Let's not get emotional, the gloves are off," said Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi on Thursday, adding that the authorities had the capacity to deal with the killings.
In a statement on Thursday, South African police said the recent rise in serious and violent crimes against women remained a "matter of grave concern", urging women in the country to remain vigilant about their personal safety.
They advised women to avoid walking alone or using isolated routes, remain alert to strangers and suspicious vehicles, and share their location or travel plans with someone they trust. They also advised against walking with earphones or earbuds at high volume, warning this could reduce awareness of their surroundings.
"Practising personal safety measures can save lives."
Authorities have offered a 400,000 rand ($24,000; £18,000) reward for information that could lead to arrests and have appealed to families with missing relatives to help identify the remaining victims.
The discoveries have caused widespread alarm in Ekurhuleni, particularly around Kempton Park, and come against the backdrop of longstanding concern about high levels of violence against women in South Africa.
Police say they are not linking the deaths to a serial killer at this stage, but are investigating the possibility that a group of people is behind the killings.
Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has cautioned against speculation, saying investigators were dealing with what appeared, at this stage, to be "quite distinct, separate events".
South Africa experiences some of the world's highest levels of gender-based violence (GBV), with the rate at which women are killed five times higher than the global average, according to UN Women.
Last November, the country classified violence against women a national disaster following an online campaign that culminated in countrywide protests.

Listed NBFC Kissht has secured board approval to raise up ₹832.2 Cr via a preferential issue of equity shares to 34 investors and entities. In a filing with the exchanges, the company said that its board has approved the issuance of 2.6 Cr fully paid-up equity shares to the investors at an issue price of ₹314.11 apiece. The NBFC did not disclose how it plans to utilise the fresh proceeds from the issue. The allotment is still subject to regulatory and shareholder approval. The company has also convened an extraordinary general meeting of the shareholders to seek approval for the preferential issue. “Funds raising by way of a preferential issue on a private placement basis of up to 2,64,93,882 fully paid-up equity shares of the company… for cash, at an issue price of ₹314.11 per share… for an amount aggregating to ₹832.19 Cr to identified investors (non-promoters), in accordance with the provisions of… applicable laws….,” read the filing. Among the investing companies, Axis Flexi Cap Fund, Axis Multi Cap Fund and Axis Small Cap Fund together will receive 63.7 Lakh shares worth nearly ₹200 Cr. Massachusetts Institute of Technology, via two entities, will also receive 27.1 Lakh shares totalling ₹85 Cr. Envision Capital will also get 12.7 Lakh shares valued at nearly ₹40 Cr, while PE firm First Bridge will lap up 12.1 Lakh shares for a sum of ₹20 Cr. Kissht will also allot 23.9 Lakh shares to three entities linked to Ashoka WhiteOak Capital for a consideration of nearly ₹75 Cr. Other investors that will receive allotment under the preferential issue include 360 One, Alchemy Capital, Groww, Bandhan Small Cap Fund, Unity Small Finance Bank, among others. In terms of the other individual investors, Ameeta Rajendra Naik will receive 63,671 shares worth ₹2 Cr and Anil Shah will get 1.6 Lakh shares valued at nearly ₹5 Cr. The latest fundraise comes barely four months after the NBFC made a strong debut on the exchanges, listing at a premium of 11.7% on the BSE compared to its issue price of ₹171. Its public issue comprised a fresh issue of shares worth ₹850 Cr and an OFS component totalling ₹76 Cr. Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, Kissht is a lending tech platform that offers digital personal and business loans of up to ₹5 Lakh. It also offers health-related insurance products and secured loans through loans against property. In July, it also received regulatory approval to begin distribution of mutual funds through its wholly-owned subsidiary Invincible Minds. The NBFC claimed to have 45+ active lending and co-lending partners under its belt at the end of June 2026. It also operated 101 offline branches across eight states and union territories, and managed to more than double YoY its active customer base to 3.49 Mn in Q1 FY27. On the financial front, Kissht’s consolidated net profit zoomed 59% to ₹95.1 Cr in Q1 FY27 as against ₹59.7 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, operating revenue zoomed nearly 45% to ₹669.5 Cr during the quarter under review as against ₹463.1 Cr in Q1 FY26. Shares of the NBFC closed Thursday’s trading session 5.08% higher at ₹359.7 on the BSE.

WASHINGTON — Health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on Thursday named eight new members to the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, an influential panel of experts who assess the evidence behind a wide array of preventive medical services.
They include a number of specialists, including in clinical nutrition, gastroenterology, and oncology, as well as a finance professor who has expertise in health insurance. It’s a major departure from the past, when the panel was made up of generalists, as opposed to specialists, to avoid prioritizing one area of medicine over another.
The independent body has more than advisory power because its assessments help determine whether health insurance companies are required to cover preventive services, such as mammograms and drugs to help prevent HIV. The newly appointed chair, Seth Corey, works in pediatric hematology-oncology at the Cleveland Clinic. He replaces Michael Silverstein, who departed from his role last year.
Kennedy has been critical of the 16-person group, which has been left with at least eight vacancies this year after five members rolled off at the end of their terms and the previous chair, Silverstein, departed on his own. Two members — vice chairs John Wong and Esa Davis — were fired in letters sent to them by Kennedy on May 11. The letters, viewed by STAT, said they were terminated due to a review of the current appointments.
The panel hasn’t met in more than a year, after its meetings were canceled by Kennedy. The most recent news on the USPSTF website dates back to August 2025. The group had previously signaled it was working on recommendations related to breast cancer genetic screening, pediatric autism disorder screening, and cervical cancer screening, among others.
Last year Kennedy said he planned to remove panel members, viewing them as too “woke,” but no new members had been named until now. His ability to remove members may be traced to a Supreme Court ruling issued in 2025, in the case Kennedy v. Braidwood Management, which established that the expert task force is under the authority of the health secretary.

On dinner timing, weight management, emerging research, pain, disease prevention, healthcare gaps and more
(In the weekly Health Matters newsletter, Athira Elssa Johnson writes about getting to good health, and staying there. You can subscribe here to get the newsletter in your inbox.)
What we eat, when we eat and how we manage our weight remain important questions in health, even as advice often runs ahead of the evidence. This week,I examine one deceptively simple question: is there a right time to have dinner?
Does eating late really affect our health? Is the time at which we eat more important than what we eat? And how should dinner timing be considered alongside sleep, work schedules, physical activity and the overall quality of the diet? Doctors explain what we know about meal timing, and what it can and cannot tell us about maintaining good health.
Close on the nutrition and weight-management front is a study from the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition, which looks at what works better for lasting weight loss. The study finds that combining diet and exercise is more effective for sustained weight loss than either approach alone. The findings are a useful reminder that weight management cannot be reduced to one food, one nutrient or one short-term intervention.
Meanwhile, the focus on protein continues to grow, particularly on social media. But increasing protein intake is not, by itself, a definition of a healthy diet. Ramya Kannan looks at what constitutes a wholesome meal and the importance of considering the overall dietary pattern rather than focusing on individual nutrients or products.
Emerging research
From everyday nutrition, we move to some interesting areas of emerging research.
Researchers are exploring whether material derived from menstrual blood could have applications in the treatment of osteoarthritis. A recent study as reported by Manjeera Gowravaram examined extracellular vesicles derived from menstrual blood stromal cells and their effects on processes involved in cartilage formation. The findings are from laboratory research and do not establish a treatment for osteoarthritis, but they add to growing interest in regenerative approaches to cartilage damage.
Another study reported by Anirban Mukhopadhyay takes a closer look at the genetic basis of cerebral palsy. Researchers found that far fewer genes may have a clear and reproducible association with the condition than some earlier studies had suggested. Understanding which genetic findings hold up is important not only for research but also for how clinicians interpret genetic information in people with cerebral palsy.
Diagnosis and care
There are also important questions about what happens within the healthcare system after patients seek care.
Dr. Suvira Jain writes about why one in three donated corneas is wasted. Eye donation does not automatically translate into transplantation. The cornea has to be retrieved, assessed, preserved and transplanted within the appropriate window. Gaps at different stages can mean that donated tissue is ultimately not used, even as many people continue to wait for corneal transplants.
Pain, too, can persist long after the original injury or illness has apparently healed. Persistent pain may require specialised assessment rather than being dismissed as something a patient simply has to live with. Afshan Yasmeen looks at why persistent pain can be complex and why appropriate pain management needs to go beyond treating the original condition.
Prevention and public health
On the disease prevention front, rabies remains an important public-health concern. Maya C. reports a study from Keralam that looks at the potential impact of dog vaccination in preventing rabies, underlining the importance of controlling the disease in its animal reservoirs alongside ensuring timely post-exposure care for people. Rabies prevention cannot depend on treating people after exposure alone; sustained vaccination and surveillance of dogs are central to controlling transmission.
The issue of counterfeit medicines also highlights why the quality and safety of healthcare products matter. A large stock of suspected counterfeit medicines was seized from a private facility in Bengaluru. Such cases raise concerns that go beyond regulation: a medicine that does not contain what it claims to contain, or does not meet required quality standards, can result in treatment failure and expose patients to further harm.
Air pollution remains another persistent health concern. A study examining winter pollution in north India finds that western disturbances explain a substantial share of the year-to-year variation in winter pollution. Weather systems are only one part of the pollution story, but understanding their role can improve forecasting and help strengthen public-health responses during periods when pollution levels are expected to rise.
Muscle metabolism, healthy ageing
For this month’s Nobel feature we look back at the work of Archibald V. Hill and Otto Meyerhof, whose Nobel-winning research helped establish how muscles generate and use energy. Their independent work helped explain fundamental aspects of muscle metabolism and the relationship between oxygen use, energy production and muscular activity.
And Health Wrap, Episode 50 looks at longevity and the role of racquet sports in healthy ageing, Navin Gnanasekaran, longevity physician and head of radiology, Apollo Hospitals, talk about healthspan, nutrition, sleep, muscle strength, stress, metabolism, inflammation and cognition. The conversation also looks at how racquet sports can bring together physical activity, social interaction and cognitive engagement, making them an interesting part of a broader discussion on maintaining health as we age.
And more:
Shanthi Dass looks at why physiotherapy matters, and the role rehabilitation can play in helping people recover function and manage health conditions.
Dr. Jyoti Bajpai writes about melanoma in India, and why the messaging around this potentially serious skin cancer needs to change to encourage earlier recognition.
Dr. Shivika Gupta looks at what to eat in the weeks before egg retrieval, addressing nutrition in the period leading up to an IVF procedure.
Bindu Shajan Perappadan reports on a WHO-linked study examining smoking and infertility, including the evidence on how quitting smoking can make a meaningful difference.
And in Keralam, health officials have sounded a caution as rising temperatures coincide with a fresh wave of fever cases in Ernakulam, another reminder of how seasonal and environmental changes can intersect with public health.

An iOS 27 bug can temporarily freeze your iPhone
Here’s how to fix it.
If you're here because your newly updated iPhone suddenly froze while you were using it, don't panic. There's an iOS 27 bug that can temporarily freeze your phone if you happen to do a series of swipes. As 9to5Mac notes, it's not going to ruin your device permanently, and you can get out of by doing a force restart. A force reboot is the first thing you should do when you're troubleshooting issues with any device, as it will clear your RAM and close programs that could be causing you problems.
Since your iPhone is frozen, and you can't access the power icon, you'll have to press and quickly release the volume up button and then do the same with the volume down button. Afterward, press and hold the side button until the Apple logo appears, and you know your phone is going through a restart. Take note that you may have to press on that button for more than 10 seconds.
In case you haven't encountered the bug yet and were wondering how it's triggered, it's by swiping down the Notification Center and the Control Center in quick succession. You'll then see buttons and icons stuck at the top of the screen, and you'll find your iPhone unable to register your swipes and taps. Apple will likely roll out a fix for this in the future, but for now, you may want to memorize our instructions for force restarts above.

In Summary
- New Apple CEO, John Ternus, announced a range of products at the Surprise and Shine event.
- While most of the focus was on the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable phone, there was much more to the event than just devices and a CEO debut.
- We bring you eight takeaways that were buried in the buzz around the new devices, which might have escaped your attention.
It might not have surprised too many people – the leaks messed that up – but Apple did a fair bit of shining at its recent Surprise and Shine event. The event, which also marked John Ternus’ debut as Apple CEO at a launch, went on expected lines, with Apple revealing new AirPods, Apple Watches, new iPhone Pros and, of course, the iPhone Duo, which has grabbed the most attention. There was, however, much more to the event than just the launches. Here are our eight biggest takeaways from the day on which the world saw Apple’s new foldable and the CEO on stage:
Table of Contents
New Era? Presentation-wise, Apple is still Cook-ing (Pun intended)
Yes, it was John Ternus who held the reins at Surprise and Shine. But in terms of presentation style, the template that was followed was still from the menu of the preceding chef, Tim Cook. We had multiple speakers, elaborate backdrops, and a similar race through a number of products, leaving the most time for the star of the show (it was the Air last time around, the Duo this time). Yes, in terms of presentation style, Apple remains well ahead of the competition, although we miss the wit and humor of the past; this launch was more from the Cook manual than the Ternus one.
No surprises (Sigh)…
It’s been a while since Apple surprised the Dickens out of us at a launch, but in recent years, the brand’s product announcements have often been leaked out well in advance. And that was pretty much true this time around. From the iPhone Duo to the shades of Burgundy to the fact that there would be no suffix-less iPhone at the event, the leak community got a lot of things right, which, as we have said in the past, takes some of the mystique and surprise out of the event. Mind you, Apple did pull one rabbit out of its hat.
…except for the AirPods 5
There were no suffix-less iPhones at Surprise and Shine, but there sure were suffix-less AirPods. And while most of the noise was about Apple’s first foldable, the AirPods 5 might have emerged as the silent, value-for-money heroes of the show. While most people had been expecting new AirPods Pro with perhaps a camera built into them, Apple brought in a new version of the classic AirPods, complete with better ANC and battery life, even while retaining the “open” fit and, surprise, surprise, the same price tag as its predecessors. Not too many noticed…until the price of the Duo was announced, and suddenly a device with no price increase became the belle of the tech ball.
Hooray, we will now have TWO iPhone launches every year
Surprise and Shine marked the beginning of a new iPhone era, in which Apple will release its iPhones in two tranches over a twelve-month period. While Apple has released iPhones at two different times of the year in the past, the second launch has generally been a relatively low-profile and soft one (of the SE and ‘e’ mainly). That is set to change now. Even if Apple does a soft launch for the iPhone 18, the iPhone Air 2 and the iPhone 18e, rather than a full-fledged event, the fact is that close to half of the iPhone portfolio will be launched in the second half of the year, and the remainder in the first half of the next year. The iPhone schedules just got tweaked.
Apple is getting REALLY serious about AI (no, really, this time)
Two years ago, Apple launched the iPhone 16 series, saying it had been designed from the ground up for Apple’s avatar of AI, Apple Intelligence. However, AI is one area where the Cupertino brand has been found trailing the competition. So it was not surprising that the brand was clearly out to write a new chapter at Surprise and Shine. Every device it announced – iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods – had a strong element of AI, which different presenters stressed would work wonderfully well, even while preserving the users’ security. Well, we have heard that a few times in the past, but never in such a comprehensive manner. Is Apple finally going to crack the AI puzzle? Based on what we saw, it would be no Surprise if it went on to Shine in that department in the coming months.
Whoop, Whoop, the Apple Watch is now a full-fledged fitness and health device, and is targeting Whoop
It started out trying to be a computer on your wrist, complete with apps, notifications and alerts, but the Apple Watch has of late graduated (or been demoted, depending on your perspective) to being mainly a health and fitness tracking device. And Surprise and Shine saw this trend continuing, with most of the talk about the Apple Watch 4 Ultra and Apple Watch Series 12 revolving around better sensors and measurement. The highlighting of features like Readiness Scores and Health Age seems to indicate that the Cupertino brand now has the screenless Whoop, which popularised these features, in its sights.
The narrative is unmatched, but is now very hardware-driven!
Processors, camera apertures, health sensors, ANC, battery life…these formed the major part of the narrative around Surprise and Shine, showing how Apple’s has shifted from storytelling to specs at its launches in recent times. This might be fine for some, but we do miss the time when an announcer would walk us through nuances of design and amazing (or they called amazing, and often, unbelievable) features on devices.
Yes, Apple remains the lord, master, and commander of product launches, but we prefer tales to tech, and a live presenter on stage to edited videos, no matter how sleekly edited. The fact that the Duo section stood out from the others because of its stress on design and UI only reinforces our belief that Apple might perhaps reconsider going back to its storytelling roots, and leave the specs on the spec sheet, rather than on the speech notes. Everyone else talks specs anyway.
Cosmic orange is out of the Apple cosmos… and Black is back!
This was so typically Apple. After making orange the color of the last twelve months, courtesy of the Cosmic Orange variant of the iPhone 17 Pro series, and making a number of brands come out with orange phones and other devices (JBL even had a pair of headphones in orange), the Cupertino giant pushed the shade out of its color palette. It also brought back the one color that everyone had missed in the Pro series – Black. Henry “Any Color As Long As It Is Black” Ford and AC/DC would approve of the return of the color, and so do we. We are not shedding any tears for orange, although we suspect those orange Pros are going to have great antique value some day.
And one more thing…
Craig Federighi’s hair looks as awesome as ever!

India’s senior living market is expected to become a $ 10.1 billion opportunity by 2030, requiring $ 7.7 billion capital investment to meet new supply under a policy-driven scenario, according to a ASLI-JLL report “India’s Silver Economy: From Niche to Necessity”.
“With over 166 million Indians aged above 60 and the number projected to double by 2050, there is a need to build an ecosystem of senior citizens. The organised senior living facility penetration is just 1.5%. The opportunity is about building a strong, accessible, and trusted senior care ecosystem,” G. Rajagopal, chairman of the Association of Senior Living India (ASLI), said in a press release.
The addressable market of urban, financially independent senior households in India is expected to grow from 1.7 million in 2026 to 2.1 million by 2030. The opportunity is not just in senior living friendly properties and communities but includes assisted care, healthcare, specialised care, rehabilitation, and other supporting services, says the report.
The organised senior living sector reached 25,050 dwelling units as of June 2026 (at 1.5 %) compared with 6-7 % in the U.S. and 14-15% in New Zealand. The sector registered 14.2 % CAGR between 2024 and first half of 2026.
“We are looking at a market that could scale from 25,050 units to 74,000 units by 2030, unlocking $ 7.7 billion in capital deployment. But the real story is not just independent living, it is the assisted living crisis. We have barely 2,100 assisted living beds today against a projected need of 11,000 by 2030, while the population of 75 plus years is growing at 7.8% annually,” said Karan Singh Sodi, Senior Managing Director, JLL.
However, despite 80 % – 85% occupancy at well-managed facilities, skilled caregiver shortages and high real estate costs remain key constraints. Affordability is a critical barrier, according to the report.
Rental and service-led models are likely to gain significant traction in the coming years, with rental models expected to overtake outright sales. Financial innovations such as repositioned Reverse Mortgage Loans and insurance-linked products could help convert existing assets into viable funding mechanisms for senior care.
The Maharashtra Housing Policy 2025 has formally recognised senior housing through dedicated planning standards and healthcare linkages, while Haryana’s policy combines licensing clarity with Floor Area Ratio incentives to improve project feasibility. Such policy measures can take the market penetration to nearly 2.4 % within four years.
Operators are also investing in digital health infrastructure, including electronic health records, monitoring wearables and telemedicine, alongside quality and accreditation frameworks, the report said.

How an Aston Villa fringe player became Europe's most prolific scorer
- Published
Just eight months ago, Donyell Malen was struggling to make a significant impact at Aston Villa.
Today, no player in Europe's top five leagues has scored more goals since his Roma debut on 18 January.
The Netherlands international has enjoyed a remarkable turnaround since joining Roma, transforming from a player who struggled to establish himself in the Premier League into one of the continent's most productive forwards.
Europe's hottest scorer
Since his Roma debut, Malen has scored 20 goals, more than Harry Kane (16), Lamine Yamal (15) and anyone else in the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 during the same period.
He also leads the way for combined goals and assists with 22, ahead of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (20), Barcelona's teenage sensation Lamine Yamal (19) and Bayern striker Kane (18).
No player across Europe's top five leagues has made a greater contribution in front of goal.
Why Roma's system suits him?
The contrast with his time at Villa could hardly be greater.
In 46 appearances for the Premier League club, the 27-year-old scored 10 goals and registered two assists. Since joining Roma, he has scored 21 goals and provided three assists in just 25 matches.
His scoring rate has improved from one goal every 149.8 minutes at Villa to one every 96.7 minutes in Rome.
On the surface, the figures suggest two very different versions of the same player. But Roma's success with Malen may owe as much to how he is being used as to any change in confidence or form.
The Dutchman arrived in Italy with a proven goalscoring pedigree and the data suggests Roma have found a role that maximises his attacking instincts.
While confidence and form may have played a part, a change in position appears to be a major factor behind the resurgence.
At Villa, Malen was often used across the frontline and spent only 52% of his league minutes as a central striker. At Roma, 99% of his Serie A minutes have come through the middle under manager Gian Piero Gasperini, making him the focal point of the attack and placing him where he can do the most damage.
The stats are backed up by the eye test. After Roma's 1-1 Champions League draw with Fenerbahce last Thursday, when Malen set up his side's goal, French football journalist Julien Laurens told Match of the Day the Dutchman had become central to Gasperini's plans.
"He has been incredible since January," said Laurens.
"He has been really efficient, super clinical. Malen is at the heart of everything they do with the ball."
Following a familiar Serie A trend
Malen is not the only former Premier League player to have flourished in Italy.
Former Manchester United midfielder Scott McTominay has thrived since swapping Old Trafford for Naples. Since joining Napoli in August 2024, only five players have scored more Serie A goals than the Scotland international's 22.
His impact has been such that Napoli supporters have even erected a street shrine in his honour.
Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund has also enjoyed an upturn in fortunes. His time in north west England divided opinion among supporters and pundits alike.
But since his Napoli debut, only Federico Dimarco, Lautaro Martinez and Malen have recorded more goal involvements than the Denmark international (19).
Their success highlights how a move to Serie A can provide players with the opportunity to thrive in a different environment and role.
For Malen, however, the transformation has been particularly dramatic.
Rather than changing Malen's game, Roma appear to have found a role that gets the best out of him. Used almost exclusively as a striker, the Dutchman has responded by producing the kind of form that first brought him to the attention of Europe's biggest clubs.
For a player whose Premier League spell failed to meet expectations, his resurgence in Italy's capital ranks among the most notable revivals in European football this year.

New passport rule sets five-year validity for children under 15, revises fee
The new regulations, notified through the Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026, came into force immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette on Sept 15.
The Ministry of External Affairs has amended passport rules to specify that an ordinary passport issued to a child below 15 years of age, containing 36 pages, will be valid for five years from the date of issue or until the child turns 18, whichever is earlier.
Signed by Joint Secretary and Chief Passport Officer BS Mubarak, the new regulations, notified through the Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026, came into force immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette on September 15.
The amendment was made under the provisions of the Passports Act, 1967. It modifies Rule 12 of the Passports Rules, 1980, which deals with the validity of passports issued to minors.
Under the newly substituted Sub-Rule (1A) of Rule 12, a 36-page ordinary passport issued to a child under 15 years of age will now remain valid for 5 years from the date of issue or until the child turns 18, whichever comes first.
However, if the child reaches the age of 18 before the five-year period expires, the passport will cease to be valid when the holder turns 18. This means the actual validity will depend on the child’s age at the time the passport is issued.
For example, if a passport is issued to a child at the age of 14, it would ordinarily be valid for five years, up to the age of 19. However, since the child will turn 18 four years after the passport is issued, the passport will cease to be valid when the child turns 18. It will therefore not remain valid from the ages of 18 to 19.
Earlier, the rule directed that an ordinary passport for a child below the age of 15 years, containing thirty-six pages shall be in force for a period of 5 years from the date of its issue or until the child attains the age of 15 years, whichever is earlier.

Changes in application fees
The notification also makes a change to Rule 8 concerning passport application fees. Amendments to Rule 8 (1) mandate that fee structures across all application types strictly adhere to the updated rates specified in Schedule IV of the Passports Rules, 1980.
The amendment replaces the existing wording to provide that fees for different types of applications will be charged at the rates specified against the corresponding applications in Schedule IV of the Rules.
These changes amend the foundational Passports Rules, 1980, which were recently updated in June 2026.
‘Passport-services related fees’
MEA had earlier revised passport fees across categories, with the new rates that came into effect from July 1. Under the revised fee structure, the cost of a fresh or reissued 36-page passport for adults will increase from ₹1,500 to ₹2,500, while the fee for a 60-page passport will rise from ₹2,000 to ₹3,500.
The Tatkaal fee for a 36-page passport was also revised to ₹5,000 from the current ₹3,500, while a 60-page passport under the Tatkaal scheme will cost ₹6,000 instead of ₹4,000.

Razer refreshes the one-handed Tartarus Pro keyboard with improved switches
There's also an analog thumbpad.
Razer just introduced the Tartarus V2 Pro, a refresh of its popular one-handed gaming keyboard thingamajig. This is one of those ergonomic designs that features an adjustable palm rest. It's also not quite a keyboard in the conventional sense. It includes over 30 keys and buttons, but they're all programmable. There's no traditional QWERTY layout here.
In any event, the V2 Pro features several upgrades over its predecessor. The optical switches have been upgraded, the keys have a wider actuation (depth) range and the thumbpad is now an analog TMR design.
The device also integrates with some new proprietary input controls. Each button can access something called Snap Flex, which lets users attach two keys to a single press. This should make it easier to pull off multi-key actions with consistency.
There's also Snap Tap, which is pretty much the opposite of Snap Flex. It ensures that two selected keys are never actuated at the same time. This is pretty useful for FPS players who like to strafe, as putting in a reverse directional input at the very moment they stop moving can often lead to both keys accidentally being pushed at once. This can cancel the strafe and leave the avatar standing there motionless like a doofus.
As with the previous version, the Tartarus V2 Pro includes an adjustable wrist-rest. Each key also boasts RGB lighting for custom aesthetics. Finally, each and every of the 31 keys and buttons are fully programmable via the company's Synapse software. It's available right now and costs $200.

Trump puts himself on the ballot
Checking in on Trump’s midterms strategy.
Welcome to The Logoff: With fewer than 50 days until the midterm elections, President Donald Trump is hitting the campaign trail.

Speaking near Charlotte, Trump urged voters to “pretend I’m on the ticket, because essentially I am.” It’s becoming a familiar refrain for the president, but not necessarily a promising one — polls suggest Trump is deeply unpopular with voters right now, more likely to drag a ticket down than boost it.
How else is Trump getting involved in the midterms? Last week, we noted that Trump was beginning to spend from his vast super PAC account to support Republican candidates. Now, we’re getting a better idea of what that spending looks like: As of earlier this week, Trump’s MAGA Inc. super PAC and related entities had booked ads to the tune of $138 million, a number that could continue to grow.
MAGA Inc. has around $400 million in the bank, though as the Washington Post reported earlier this month, Trump has a long list of other things he could choose to spend that money on instead of the midterms (such as legal fees, travel, or even his eventual presidential library).
Will it make a difference? It’s a whole lot of money. But with not much time left until voters go to the polls and some mail-in ballots already going out — North Carolina voters began receiving theirs earlier this month — the map is looking fairly dire for Republican hopes.
Trump, meanwhile, isn’t doing himself any favors. The fuel shortages caused by the Iran war are only getting worse, as my colleague Caitlin Dewey explained today. Polls suggest he’s picked the wrong side of the AI issue. And voters are still extremely mad about inflation.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

China on Thursday (September 17) rejected the US use of tariffs to pressure countries over their purchases of Russian oil and gas, saying Beijing would not accept Washington’s “long-arm jurisdiction” or interference in its normal trade and economic cooperation.
The warning came after the US House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act 2026, which authorises President Donald Trump to impose sanctions on Russia and steep tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy, including China and India.
The legislation, already passed by the US Senate, cleared the House in a 262-159 vote and will now go to Trump for his signature.
Quick answers to key questions
China opposes US tariffs on Russian oil purchases because it believes such measures constitute 'long-arm jurisdiction' and disrupt its normal trade and economic cooperation with other nations.
China's Foreign Ministry emphasizes that it rejects unilateral sanctions that lack authorization from the UN Security Council, asserting that its trade relations are based on equality and mutual benefit.
US tariffs could significantly affect India's energy imports from Russia by increasing costs and potentially reducing the volume of crude oil purchased, amid India's reliance on Russian oil to meet its energy needs.
India is committed to ensuring its energy security and is exploring diversified sourcing of oil to mitigate the impact of potential US tariffs on its imports of Russian oil.
US sanctions on Russian oil could tighten the supply and increase prices in international energy markets, potentially impacting net energy importers like India, especially amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing opposes measures that lack authorisation from the UN Security Council.
“China engages in normal economic and trade cooperation with other countries on the basis of equality and mutual benefit,” Guo said at a media briefing.
“Such cooperation does not target any third party and shall be free from disruption or coercion from any third party. China opposes long-arm jurisdiction and unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and lack UN Security Council mandate,” he said.
The bill seeks sanctions not only against Russia's leadership and energy sector but also against vessels in the so-called “shadow fleet” that allegedly help Moscow evade sanctions on oil shipments.
It also authorises Trump to impose tariffs on countries including China and India in an effort to reduce their dependence on Russian oil and gas, along with additional sanctions targeting Iran.
Beijing's latest warning comes ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's planned visit to Washington for a summit with Trump, expected on September 24-25.
The meeting would be the second summit between the two leaders this year. Trump visited Beijing in May and held extensive talks with Xi.
China has repeatedly opposed unilateral sanctions and has also continued to purchase Iranian oil despite US sanctions.
China and India are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil and gas. Much of China's Russian energy imports are transported through pipelines across its land border.
Despite the dispute over Russian energy, China and the US are continuing talks on tariffs.
China's Commerce Ministry said Thursday that Beijing and Washington were consulting on a reciprocal tariff reduction framework covering $30 billion worth of products from each side.
India has separately warned that the US sanctions legislation could have implications for New Delhi-Washington ties and the global energy market, particularly because it provides for punitive tariffs of up to 100% on major Russian crude buyers.
The Ministry of External Affairs said India remains “firmly committed” to ensuring the energy security of its 1.4 billion people and would take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests.
India is monitoring developments following the passage of the legislation, the MEA said, adding that the issue has been discussed at high levels with US interlocutors in recent months.
“The government will work closely with Indian trade and industry bodies to deal with the implications of these developments,” the ministry said.

Two Britons among three killed in Swiss Alps light aircraft crash
All three occupants on board were killed when the small plane crashed high in the mountains
Three people have been killed, including two British citizens, after a plane crashed in the Swiss Alps.
The group were on board a light aircraft on Tuesday afternoon when it collided into a mountain slope ten minutes into its journey, killing all occupants on board. The victims have yet to be named and investigations into the incident are ongoing.
Authorities identified the plane as a Cirrus SR22T that had had taken off in Lugano before making a stopover at Sion Airport. It then left Sion to travel to the Rhone Valley and crashed near the town of Leukerbad in the southern canton of Valais at around 4pm.
Police said the plane had been headed towards Buochs Airfield in the canton of Nidwalden.
Signs of smoke were reported in the region raising the alarm, according to a statement by Valais police.
Emergency services including police, firefighters and three helicopters of the Valais Rescue Organisation rushed to the scene of the incident.
Witnesses said that fire and smoke were visible at the site of the crash. An image released by Valais Police show smoke rising from the locations as emergency workers attended the scene.
The reason for the crash is yet to be determined and the Swiss Transportation Board has opened an investigation into the cause.
Valais Police and the Office of the Attorney General have also launched a criminal inquiry following the crash.
The Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office said it was “providing support to the families of two British nationals who died in Switzerland” and is in contact with local authorities, in a statement to the BBC. “Our thoughts remain with the families during this difficult time.”
The incident comes less than a week after a bus carrying 48 Dutch passengers crashed in the Swiss Alps, killing five tourists on board.
The vehicle crashed into a guardrail and overturned before sliding down a slope. At least 40 people were left injured in the incident.
Rescue helicopters airlifted the injured to various hospitals as work began to identify the dead.

Wealthy Texas suburb denies permit for church to hold a Pride event
The Southlake City Council approved the permit for the Pride event last year
City officials in Southlake, Texas, have denied a Pride festival a permit to hold an event scheduled for this October despite granting the same permit last year, according to local reports.
On Tuesday, the Southlake City Council voted to deny Pride Kel-So festival organizers a permit they are seeking for an October event, according to Fox 4.
Only two people spoke about the event during the city council meeting, with one person speaking in favor of the event and another speaking in opposition to the festival. None of the city councilors offered comment or asked the organizers any questions.
The council issued a unanimous vote against the permit. Now, the organizers are seeking an explanation.
"I am just in shock still," April Dreyson, one of the festival's co-founders, told the outlet. She said that the city council has not explained its vote despite approving the festival a year prior.
According to the festival's organizers, the inaugural Pride Kel-So festival was approved in 2025. It was held at St. Martin-in-the-Fields Episcopal Church in Southlake. The name "Kel-So" is a combination of the words Keller and Southlake, referencing the fact that the church that hosted the festival sits on the border of the two cities.
They told Fox 4 that 2,500 people attended the event, which they described as family-friendly. The festival, which celebrates the LGBT community, featured live music and vendors.
"We followed all the recommendations and did not expect, especially with no comments, no questions. If they had concerns, they didn’t bring them up," Dreyson said.
In a Facebook post after the vote, Dreyson said the only explanation for the denial she could think of is discrimination.
“There is no explanation for the city council's vote other than pure discrimination against a group of people. Zero excuse," she wrote.
The individual who spoke in support of the event was the church's associate pastor, Reverend Ellen Singer.
"It’s clear there is conflict. It’s clear there is some sort of rupture in the community and actually the goal of something like this is to bring people together, to celebrate being a community with one another," she told Fox 4.
The church's leader, Reverend Alan Bentrup, told the Fort Worth Star-Telegram that he was out of town at the time of the council meeting, but that he supports the festival and wants to host it again this year.
“We’ve been clear from the beginning that we want to [host the Pride Kel-So event]. We are willing and eager to host whatever might be possible,” Bentrup said.
The opposing voice at the city council meeting said that the festival was "abhorrent" and drew protesters to the event.
Bentrup said he had been to numerous "contentious" city council meetings and noted that it was unusual that one dissenting voice would sway the council's vote.
“One person speaking against doesn’t usually fit that,” he said.
If the council does not reconsider, the festival organizers said it could downsize the festival and limit the number of guests to 1,000 people. Any gathering of 1,000 people or more requires a permit per the city's laws.
Dreyson told Fox 4 that she and the other festival organizers would "figure it out," and has been adamant on social media that the festival will happen in one form or another.
Pilar Schank, a spokesperson for the city, declined to comment on the matter and directed The Independent to a video of the September 15 city council meeting.
